# Task: every new note is refused

Since the last release, every `POST /notes` from the mobile app is answered
`400 Bad Request`. The app has not changed: it sends what `API.md` says, for
example `{"text":"buy milk"}` with `Content-Type: application/json` and a
valid token. Reading notes still works.

Find out why and fix it.
# Notes API

The contract the notes service keeps with its clients. Every answer below is
relied on by a client; a change to one is a change to this document first.

## Every route

- A request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the scheme is matched
  in any case (`bearer` too). The service reads its tokens at start-up, one
  `token user` pair per line of its tokens file.
- A missing, malformed or unknown token: `401`, body `Unauthorized`, and the
  field `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- A note is visible to its owner only: anyone else gets the same `404` as for
  a note that does not exist.
- JSON is sent and received as `Content-Type: application/json`. A note is
  `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk"}`, its members in that order.
- A request the service cannot read (a path value that is not a number, a
  JSON body that is malformed or lacks a member) is `400`, body
  `Bad Request`, with its cause written to the service's standard error.

## Routes

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /notes` | `200`, the caller's notes, oldest first: `[{"id":1,...}]`, or `[]` |
| `GET /notes/{id}` | `200`, the note; `404`, body `no note {id}`, when there is none the caller owns |
| `POST /notes`, body `{"text":"..."}` | `201`, the note as stored, with its new id; `422`, body `text too long`, when the text is longer than the service's limit in bytes |

## Storage

Notes are kept in a journal file and read back at start-up. A note whose write
fails is not kept: the client gets `503`, body `storage unavailable`, the
cause is written to standard error, and the next write succeeds once the
journal can be written again. The next note takes the id the failed one did
not use.

## Running the service

    PROGRAM PORT JOURNAL TOKENS MAX_TEXT

`MAX_TEXT` is the longest text accepted, in bytes.
#!/bin/sh
# Builds ./notes from notes_muntin.mojo.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec /root/.pixi/bin/pixi run --manifest-path /home/user/muntin/pixi.toml --frozen -e flare mojo build -I lib -I . notes_muntin.mojo -o notes
#!/bin/sh
# Serves ./notes on 127.0.0.1:PORT (default 8080), its journal in
# journal.log, its tokens in tokens (t-ada is ada, t-bo is bo), texts
# up to 40 bytes.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec ./notes "${1:-8080}" journal.log tokens 40

# Request bodies

A typed `post`, `put` or `patch` handler takes one body, as its last parameter, after at most two route values (or one record) and after any `State` ([routing](routing.md#registering-a-route)). A body is one of:

- a `FromBody` type: text the application parses;
- `Json[T]` with `T: FromJson`: JSON parsed by Muntin's codec;
- a `FromBytes` type: the body's bytes, with a declared size limit;
- `WithHeaders[B]` around one of these: the body and the request's header fields.

The body comes from the request body only, never from the path or query, byte for byte. A conversion that raises is 400 `Bad Request` and the handler is not called; the error's text is not sent, only kept in the 400's report, which tells a body that is not UTF-8 or, for `Json[T]`, not JSON from a conversion's raise ([errors](errors.md#reports-of-rejected-requests)). The order of checks is in [routing](routing.md#order-of-checks). A handler without a body on these methods is bodyless ([routing](routing.md#bodyless-post-put-and-patch)); a raw handler reads any body itself ([raw handlers](raw.md)).

Each example below is its own `App` (named `app`, created with `var app = App()`), so the same route or type name (`POST /users`, `create_user`, `CreateUser`, `Unauthorized`) means that example's own; the line after it names the test that runs it and what that test adds or changes.

## Text bodies (`FromBody`)

<!-- example: tests/test_reference_examples.mojo#bodies-text-body -->
```mojo
from muntin import App, FromBody


struct CreateUser(FromBody):              # defined by the application; may be move-only
    var name: String

    def __init__(out self, name: String):
        self.name = name

    @staticmethod
    def from_body(body: String) raises -> Self:   # the application owns the body format
        if not body.startswith("name=") or body.byte_length() == 5:
            raise Error("expected name=<text>")
        return Self(String(body[byte=5:]))

10:The body comes from the request body only, never from the path or query, byte for byte. A conversion that raises is 400 `Bad Request` and the handler is not called; the error's text is not sent, only kept in the 400's report, which tells a body that is not UTF-8 or, for `Json[T]`, not JSON from a conversion's raise ([errors](errors.md#reports-of-rejected-requests)). The order of checks is in [routing](routing.md#order-of-checks). A handler without a body on these methods is bodyless ([routing](routing.md#bodyless-post-put-and-patch)); a raw handler reads any body itself ([raw handlers](raw.md)).
49:- Muntin reads the body's bytes as strict UTF-8 first: bytes that are not well-formed UTF-8 are 400 before `from_body`, never replaced by U+FFFD. An empty body, whitespace, NUL and a U+FFFD the client sent reach `from_body` unchanged. Text bodies have no Muntin size limit, `Json[T]` keeps its fixed 1 MiB step ([below](#json-jsont)), and raw handlers measure `req.body` themselves; the `Server`'s `max_body_bytes` applies over the wire ([serving](serving.md#receive-body-limit)).
98:## JSON (`Json[T]`)
100:The application wraps its own type in `Json[T]`, which is a body and a [result](responses.md#json-results); registration is unchanged. A struct that conforms to `JsonFields` is read and written from its fields:
102:<!-- example: tests/test_json_dx.mojo#bodies-json-derived -->
104:from muntin import App, Json, JsonFields
108:struct NewNote(JsonFields):       # a JSON object, one member per field, named after it
115:struct Note(JsonFields):
122:def create_note(body: Json[NewNote]) -> Json[Note]:
124:    return Json(Note(1, n.text, n.tags.copy(), n.due), status=201)
127:def import_notes(body: Json[List[NewNote]]) -> Json[List[Note]]:   # a top-level List
132:    return Json(notes^)
137:# POST /notes  Content-Type: application/json  {"text":"hi","tags":["a"]}
138:#   -> 201, Content-Type: application/json, {"id":1,"text":"hi","tags":["a"],"due":null}
141:# {"tags":[]} -> 400 "Bad Request"; its Rejection: from_json: text: JSON member is missing
142:# [{"text":"a","tags":[1]}] -> 400; its Rejection: from_json: [0].tags[0]: JSON value is not a string
145:Run by `tests/test_json_dx.mojo` (`test_derived_json_example`), as written; it also posts a `null` `due`, read as empty. Every kind, ownership, a hand-written direction and each failure's report on a bare, carried, guarded and stateful body: `tests/test_derived_json.mojo`.
147:- A field is an `Int`, `Float64`, `Bool`, `String`, a `FromJson` type (read) or `ToJson` type (written), a `JsonFields` struct, or a `List` or `Optional` (not of an `Optional`) of one. Its member is named after it (`` var `created-at`: Int `` is `created-at`); there is no renaming or default: for those, write that direction by hand (below).
149:- `Json[T]` also takes a top-level `List` or `Optional` of any of these, as a body and as a result (`Json[Optional[Note]]` reads and writes `null` as empty).
150:- **`JsonFields` is for a receiving DTO: a struct for which any combination of field values is valid to hold, use and destroy.** Muntin builds it without running any of its initializers; conforming consents to that, as for [`RouteValues`](route-values.md#route-value-records). What `__init__` guarantees does not hold: a `Range` whose `__init__` requires `start <= end` is built from `{"start":10,"end":0}`, and its methods and destructor see that value, even after the handler rejects it. A type with an invariant does not conform: read a DTO, check it, and build the type with its own constructor, or read the type with a hand-written `from_json` that checks and constructs. A failure part-way destroys each field already read, once; the struct's destructor does not run.
151:- A hand-written `FromJson` or `ToJson` on the struct takes that direction over. The reverse does not work: a hand-written `write_json` cannot write a `JsonFields` value (`out.field` takes `ToJson` types: `no matching method in call to 'field'`), and `from_json` has no derived reader to call.
152:- A field that cannot be read (a body) or written (a result) is refused at the registration, naming the innermost one: `constraint failed: field zip of the JsonFields struct <module>.Place has type SIMD[DType.uint8, 1], which cannot be read: a derived field is an Int, Float64, Bool, String, a FromJson type, a JsonFields struct, or a List or Optional of one`; a raw handler's `Json[T].from_body` is refused alike where it is called. Another top-level type is `Json[<type>] cannot be read` (or `written`). Not supported: `Dict`, other widths (`Int64`, `Float32`), `Optional[Optional[T]]`, and a struct holding a `List` of itself (Mojo 1.1.0 rejects the struct).
153:- A body that does not read is 400, and its [report](errors.md#reports-of-rejected-requests)'s message starts with the member path (`notes[2].text: JSON value is not a string`, `[0].tags[0]: ...`); a top-level value of the wrong kind has none. `Json[T].from_body` raises the same text.
155:### Hand-written codecs (`FromJson`, `ToJson`)
157:For another representation (renamed or defaulted members, a check while reading), the application declares `FromJson`/`ToJson` on its own type:
159:<!-- example: tests/test_json_dx.mojo#bodies-json -->

165:struct CreateUser(FromJson):
171:    def from_json(value: JsonValue) raises -> Self:   # raise -> 400, handler not called
180:struct User(ToJson):
184:    def write_json(self, mut out: JsonWriter) raises:  # raise -> fixed 500, not the handler's error
191:def create_user(body: Json[CreateUser]) -> Json[User]:    # borrow and read body.value
192:    return Json(User(1, body.value.name))
195:def replace_user(id: Int, var body: Json[CreateUser]) -> Json[User]:
197:    return Json(User(id, c.name))

203:#   -> 200, Content-Type: application/json, {"id":1,"name":"Ada"}
204:# Content-Type missing, text/plain, two fields, or application/problem+json
205:#   -> 415 "Unsupported Media Type" (before parsing and the handler)
207:# application/json; charset=utf-8 -> accepted (parameters are not interpreted)
208:# malformed JSON, a missing member, a wrong kind -> 400 "Bad Request"

It does not check that 415 is answered before 413.
213:- `value[name]` raises naming the missing member (`JSON member "name" is missing`); `int()` and `float()` do not quote the literal.
215:### Rules for every JSON body
217:- `Content-Type`: exactly one field whose media type (before any `;`, trimmed) is `application/json`, ASCII case-insensitively; parameters are ignored. Missing, repeated, other and `+json` types are 415.
218:- Size: at most 1,048,576 bytes; one more is 413 (fixed). `Json[T].from_body` also raises above it in a raw handler.
221:- A `FromJson` or `JsonFields` type is not a body by itself (`def create_user(body: CreateUser)` gets the `FromBody or FromBytes` message).
224:- `TestClient.post(target, body)` sends no fields, so it gets 415; send `headers=` with the `Content-Type` ([testing](testing.md)).

input.message:
**What was wrong:** the request DTO for `POST /notes` had the wrong field name. In `notes_muntin.mojo`, `NewNote` was declared as `var content: String`. Muntin's `JsonFields` names each JSON member after its field and has no renaming (docs/reference/bodies.md, "JSON"). So the service required `{"content":"..."}`, and the `{"text":"..."}` that API.md specifies was turned away before the handler ran with `400 Bad Request`. The service's stderr showed the cause: `rejected: POST /notes from_json: content: JSON member is missing`. Before the fix I sent the same request with `{"content":...}` and got 201, which confirmed it. Reading notes was unaffected because `NoteJson` already uses `text`.

**Fix:** I renamed the field to `var text: String`, added a one-line comment tying it to API.md, and changed `create_note` to read `body.value.text`. API.md needed no change: the service now matches the contract again.

**Files changed:** only `/srv/runs/r23/notes_muntin.mojo`.

**Verification:** `./build.sh` succeeds. Against the running service (ports 20230–20232):
- `{"text":"buy milk"}` with `Bearer t-ada` gets 201 `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk"}`.
- `bearer` and `BEARER` schemes are accepted.
- A 40-byte text gets 201; a 41-byte text gets 422 `text too long`.
- Malformed JSON and `{}` get 400, with their causes on stderr.
- A missing or unknown token gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- Another user's note and a missing note get 404 `no note N`; `/notes/abc` gets 400.
- `GET /notes` lists the caller's notes oldest first.
- After a restart, notes are read back from the journal.

I stopped every server I started, by its process id, and removed my temporary `work/` directory. The only file left from my work is the built `./notes`. Another `notes` process on port 20151 (pid 12465) belongs to someone else, so I left it running.

**Unsure of / not verified:** I could not trigger the 503 `storage unavailable` path:
- Pointing the journal at a directory makes the service fail at start-up while reading it, in `store.mojo`.
- Renaming the journal's directory while the service was running did not make the write fail: the write still succeeded.

That path was untouched by this fix, so I didn't pursue it further.
